prompt: Build Budget Ledger, a personal budget tracker that runs as one self-contained HTML page with no server, no build step and no libraries. A tab bar across the top switches between twelve views, one per feature. Transactions: add income and expenses with a date, description, category and amount, delete any of them, and have an invalid entry refused with a message. Balance: income, expenses and the resulting balance. Categories: what was spent per category, largest first. Monthly: pick a month and see only that month. Search: filter the list by description as you type. Sorting: order the list by date, amount or description, either direction. Budgets: a monthly limit per category with spent, remaining and an over-budget warning. Recurring: a rule that repeats on a day of the month, with its occurrences posted into the ledger. Export: the ledger as CSV text. Import: paste CSV and add its rows. Chart: a bar chart of spending by category. Saved data: everything persists in the browser between visits. Expenses are negative amounts and income positive, with cents. Write your own implementation from scratch.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: budget-ledger.html, one self-contained HTML page. All 14 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. The page starts with <!doctype html>, makes zero external requests, holds a <nav> with one button[data-tab=NAME] and one <section id="panel-NAME"> per feature, and one plain <script id="app"> (not a module) that runs to completion in node with document, window and localStorage stubbed and leaves window.App.features holding one entry per feature, each with a `model` object of pure functions and a `render(root, state)` function. The twelve features, each scored by its own test test_feature_NAME: 1. transactions: the user adds a transaction with date, description, category and amount and deletes one by its id; every added transaction gets a unique id, the list the user had is not modified in place, and an invalid entry (blank description, zero or non-numeric amount, date not YYYY-MM-DD) is refused with one message per broken rule. 2. balance: the page shows income (sum of positive amounts), expenses (sum of the absolute negative amounts) and balance (income minus expenses), correct to the cent. 3. categories: spending per category for expenses only, largest total first, income never listed. 4. monthly: the months present in the ledger are listed in ascending YYYY-MM order and choosing one shows only that month's transactions. 5. search: typing in the search box keeps only transactions whose description contains the text, case-insensitive; an empty or blank box keeps everything. 6. sorting: the list can be ordered by date, amount or description, ascending or descending; description order ignores case. 7. budgets: for each category with a limit, the month's spent amount, the remaining amount (limit minus spent, negative when exceeded) and an over flag when spent exceeds the limit. 8. recurring: a rule with description, category, amount, day of month (1-28) and start date expands to one dated occurrence per month between two dates inclusive, never before its start date, in date order. 9. exporter: the ledger exports as CSV text with the header date,description,category,amount and one row per transaction; fields holding commas, quotes or line breaks are quoted with inner quotes doubled. 10. importer: pasted CSV in that same format (header first, CRLF or LF, quoted fields allowed) becomes transactions with numeric amounts. 11. chart: a bar chart of spending by category, largest first, in which the largest bar fills the given width and every other bar is proportional to its total. 12. persist: the ledger is saved to localStorage as JSON and restored on the next visit; with nothing saved, loading yields null. If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a page that games the tests.
contract: Return ONE complete HTML document in the `code` field, from <!doctype html> to </html>, saved as budget-ledger.html. Structure: 1. <head> with a <style> holding every rule; no external stylesheet. 2. <body> with a <nav id="tabs"> holding one <button data-tab="NAME"> per feature and a <main> holding one empty <section id="panel-NAME" class="panel"> per feature, in this order: transactions, balance, categories, monthly, search, sorting, budgets, recurring, exporter, importer, chart, persist. 3. One plain <script id="app"> (no type="module", no import or export) that builds a global `App` and ends with `window.App = App`. It must touch no DOM element and read no user data at load time: the gate extracts this script alone, stubs document, window, localStorage, location and history with inert objects, runs it in node and then calls the model functions listed below. Mounting (rendering every panel into its section, wiring the tabs, re-rendering on state changes, loading saved data) happens in App.mount(document), called from a second, separate <script> placed after it. 4. App.store = {get(), set(patch), subscribe(fn)} holding the state {transactions: [], budgets: {}, recurring: [], ui: {}}; set merges the patch into the state and notifies subscribers. App.router.show(name) makes section#panel-NAME and its tab active and hides the others. 5. App.features.NAME = {model: {...}, render(root, state)} for each of the twelve names. render writes the feature's whole panel into root (its section) from state and wires its own events, which change state only through App.store.set. model holds pure functions: no DOM, no localStorage (persist excepted), never mutating the arrays or objects they receive, always returning new ones. A transaction is {id, date: 'YYYY-MM-DD', description, category, amount}; amount is a number, negative for an expense and positive for income; money is compared to the cent. Model functions the gate calls, exact names and shapes: transactions.model.add(list, {date, description, category, amount}) -> new array = list plus the item carrying a unique id; transactions.model.remove(list, id) -> new array without that id; transactions.model.validate(tx) -> array of error strings, one per failing rule (description blank after trimming; amount not a finite non-zero number; date not YYYY-MM-DD), [] when valid. balance.model.totals(list) -> {income, expense, balance} with income = sum of positive amounts, expense = sum of absolute negative amounts, balance = income - expense. categories.model.byCategory(list) -> [{category, total}] for expenses only, total = sum of absolute amounts, sorted by total descending. monthly.model.months(list) -> sorted distinct 'YYYY-MM' strings; monthly.model.forMonth(list, 'YYYY-MM') -> that month's transactions in their original order. search.model.search(list, query) -> transactions whose description contains the trimmed query, case-insensitive, original order; an empty or blank query returns a copy of the whole list. sorting.model.sortBy(list, key, direction) with key one of date, amount, description and direction 'asc' or 'desc' -> new sorted array; amount compares numerically, the other keys as lower-cased strings. budgets.model.status(list, limits, 'YYYY-MM') with limits = {category: limit} -> [{category, limit, spent, remaining, over}], one per key of limits; spent = absolute expense total of that category in that month; remaining = limit - spent; over = spent > limit. recurring.model.occurrences(rule, from, to) with rule = {description, category, amount, day, start} and ISO dates from and to, both inclusive -> [{date, description, category, amount}] for every month whose day-of-month `day` falls between max(from, start) and to, ascending by date. exporter.model.toCsv(list) -> string: the header line date,description,category,amount, then one line per transaction in list order; a field containing a comma, a double quote or a line break is wrapped in double quotes with inner quotes doubled. importer.model.fromCsv(text) -> array of {date, description, category, amount} parsed from that same format (header line first, LF or CRLF line ends, quoted fields with doubled quotes), amount as a number, no id needed. chart.model.bars(list, width) -> [{category, total, width}] for expense categories, largest total first; the largest bar's width equals the given width and every other bar's width = width * total / largest total. persist.model.save(state) writes {transactions, budgets, recurring} as JSON to localStorage; persist.model.load() -> that object, or null when nothing valid was saved. Division of labour for the swarm: each of the twelve feature names owns the `// part:NAME` block holding App.features.NAME inside the app script; store owns `// part:store` (App.store); router owns `// part:router` (App.router); styles owns the `<!-- part:styles -->` block around the stylesheet; shell owns the `<!-- part:shell -->` block holding the body markup (the nav and the twelve sections). skeptic, referee, measurer and qa own no block: they review. Helpers shared by several blocks and App.mount live outside every block and stay frozen. Everything inline: no external fonts, images, scripts, stylesheets or network calls of any kind.
